changelog: Added explicit permission to split at -는데/-고/-아서/어서/니까 junctions in long multi-clause utterances when both sides already form independent, resolvable clauses — targets under-segmentation of rambling sentences flagged by critic.
Added rule to treat mid-utterance sentence-final punctuation (e.g. embedded '?') as a valid split candidate, not just end-of-text punctuation.
Added rule to split after a closing quotation / quoted clause-final question before a reporting verb (했더니, 그러더라, etc.), since the quoted clause is self-contained.

Narrowed [Never Segment] bans on -는데/-고/-아서/니까 to only apply when the following material is not yet an independently complete clause, explicitly carving out the exception where both sides already stand alone — removes over-broad prohibition that was suppressing safe splits.
